tasks.task: Site setup and occupied building interface
tasks.scope: Establish site boundaries, residents communication plan, dust control, waste management staging, toilet and welfare facilities coordination with building management.
hazards: Dust and debris migration into occupied building affecting residents
Trip and fall hazard from temporary barriers, hoses and welfare facilities in courtyard and access routes
Noise and vibration disturbance to residents during setup and work hours
Inadequate waste segregation causing cross-contamination and disposal delays
tasks.dominant_hazard: Trip and fall hazard from temporary infrastructure in shared access areas
controls: Barricade all temporary infrastructure (barriers, hoses, welfare units) with 1.2 m high barriers and 'DO NOT ENTER' signage at each courtyard and access route entry point.
Install dust suppression at source — wet all excavated material and temporary stockpiles before placement; activate water spray systems during dust-generating setup tasks.
Establish and post a residents' notice board in building foyer with: project duration, work hours, site contact, complaint hotline, and weekly activity schedule.
Coordinate with building management before setup: confirm welfare facility locations (toilet, shed), waste bin staging areas, and confirmation that all utility services are marked and isolated.
Mark all temporary hoses, cables, and trip hazards with high-visibility tape and edge protection; keep all pathways clear of equipment and materials during non-work hours.
Implement waste segregation with separate labelled bins (general, concrete, timber, metal) at waste staging area; confirm removal schedule with waste contractor before site start.
Brief all workers on occupied building interface — identify resident access routes, keep noise below 75 dB during early morning and evening, and report any resident complaints immediately.
Check that all scaffolding handover certificates are signed by the licenced scaffolder and filed on site before any worker accesses the scaffold.
Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow any worker on site until: residents' notice board is installed, welfare facilities are confirmed operational with building management, and all temporary barriers are erected.

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not erect or use any scaffold until: load calculations are certified by engineer, scaffold handover certificate is signed by licenced scaffolder, and working-at-heights permit is issued and displayed on site.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start work until: written notification delivered to all affected occupants and body corporate/strata manager
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: dust or debris is visibly migrating into occupied areas despite suppression measures — reposition suppression systems and re-test before restart.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any temporary barrier, hose, or welfare facility is missing signage, damaged, or creating a trip hazard — reinstate or remove from pathway before work resumes.
🛑 STOP WORK if: waste bins are overflowing or mixed waste is detected in segregation bins — sort and empty before any further material is added.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain signed residents' communication plan from building management; display contact details on site noticeboard.
Verify EPA licence is current and displayed on site before waste staging begins.
Obtain and file scaffold erection permit signed by licenced scaffolder; obtain working-at-heights permit before any elevated task.
Obtain noise management plan from principal contractor; confirm compliance with local council noise limits (typically 75 dB daytime, 55 dB evening/weekend).
Verify all workers hold current White Card (CPCCWHS1001) and relevant scaffolding licence (if working on scaffold) before site entry.
Brief building manager weekly on waste removal schedule and any resident complaints; record in site diary.
Check and confirm utility markings (water, power, gas, communications) are visible and building management has verified their accuracy before any excavation or ground work.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
Residents responsible for clearing personal items, furniture, potted plants, and non-common fixtures from balcony and work areas before each phase — area left/excluded if not cleared
Temporary access to neighbouring properties required — confirm access arrangements before commencing
Vegetation trimmed away from surfaces designated for painting or remedial works prior to commencement — area excluded if vegetation impedes access
On-site parking or provision of parking permits required for duration of works
Final inspection and agreed scope of works to be confirmed before commencement
ppe: High-visibility vest or shirt (AS/NZS 1906.4 Class D) — worn during all site setup activities in shared areas.
Hard hat (AS/NZS 2807.1) — worn when working on or near temporary structures, scaffolding, or welfare installations.
steel-capped footwear— worn always on site.
Dust mask (P2/FFP2) — worn during dust-generating setup tasks (material handling, suppression system setup).
High-visibility barriers and 'DO NOT ENTER' signage — installed at all temporary infrastructure entry points (not PPE, but critical interface control).

monitoring.critical_control: Check all temporary barriers are in place with legible signage before each shift start.
monitoring.frequency: before each shift start and after each major setup change
monitoring.evidence: Photographic record of barriers and signage placement; signed-off supervision log; resident complaint register (nil or documented).

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues

tasks.task: Erect scaffold to balconies via Kiora Lane and courtyard
tasks.scope: Install and certify scaffold system accessing all balconies. make sure stability, safe access, and compliance with 4m height classification. Obtain scaffold tag and certifier sign-off before any personnel work at height.
hazards: Fall from height — scaffold collapse or structural failure during assembly
Fall from height — incomplete or unstable scaffold preventing safe work at height
Dropped object from scaffold platform or tools striking persons or building below
Crush injury to workers during scaffold component handling and assembly
Contact with building facade or balustrade elements during scaffold positioning
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — scaffold collapse or failure during assembly and use
controls: Obtain signed scaffold erection permit from licenced scaffolder before any component placement begins.
Verify load calculations and design documentation match site conditions and balcony geometry.
Check all scaffold components for damage, deformation, or corrosion before assembly.
Establish exclusion zone minimum 2m radius below scaffold footprint — barricade with tape and signage.
Assemble scaffold only on level, compacted ground or approved temporary support pads.
Secure base plates, standards, and ledger beams to prevent lateral movement during erection.
Attach guardrails and toe boards to each platform as section rises — do not work on incomplete sections.
Verify all connections torqued, pinned, and locked before moving to next level.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not permit worker access to scaffold until: handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder and white card verified for all personnel
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not erect sections over 4m until: working at heights permit signed and competency verification (RIIOHS204E or equivalent) confirmed for supervisor
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold components show cracks, bending, or corrosion during assembly.
🛑 STOP WORK if: guardrails, toe boards, or edge protection removed or missing on any active platform.
🛑 STOP WORK if: ground conditions become saturated, unstable, or base support pads shift.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

Obtain handover certificate from licenced scaffolder before any personnel access scaffold.
Obtain working at heights permit signed by supervisor before elevated work commences.

tell building occupants of exclusion zones and access restrictions via notice board and verbal brief.
Record scaffold tag number and certification date on site induction board.
ppe: Fall arrest harness and lanyard (where working over edges or unsupported voids).

monitoring.critical_control: Check guardrails and toe boards present on all active platforms before shift start.
monitoring.frequency: Before each shift and after any scaffold modification.
monitoring.evidence: Visual walk-around; photo record; supervisor sign-off on site diary.

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold or EWP certification, supervise erection, sign off load checks
responsibility.WKR: Follow erection plan, wear harness at height, report defects

tasks.task: Remove existing waterproofing membrane, screed and tile bed
tasks.scope: Strip all existing membrane, screed layer and tile bed to expose concrete slab. Manage silica dust and debris control. Segregate and remove all waste off-site.
hazards: Inhalation of silica dust from grinding and cutting membrane and screed
Respiratory irritation from dust and tile particulates during removal
Cut and laceration injuries from tile shards and sharp membrane edges
Fall from height — loss of footing on wet or debris-covered scaffold platform
Noise exposure from mechanical cutting and grinding equipment
tasks.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of respirable crystalline silica dust during removal and grinding
controls: Wet-cut all membrane and screed using water suppression system — apply water continuously during cutting to suppress silica dust at source.
Use HEPA-filtered dust extraction connected directly to cutting equipment — maintain negative pressure and check filter saturation before each shift.
Wear P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) fitted and sealed before starting work — verify fit each shift using manufacturer's fit-test protocol.
Barricade work area with exclusion zone 2 metres beyond drop edge — restrict entry to authorized workers only.
Remove debris to collection bin inside exclusion zone — do not throw debris from height or allow fallout onto occupied areas below.
check scaffold platform for debris and wet surfaces before each work phase — clear debris and allow surfaces to dry before proceeding.
Segregate all asbestos-suspect material separately during removal — do not mix with general waste; hold and tell site supervisor for verification.
Wear eye protection, heavy-duty gloves and cut-resistant sleeves when handling tile shards and sharp membrane edges.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start cutting until: water suppression system is tested and running, HEPA extraction is connected and sealed, and P2 respirators are fitted to all workers.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove debris until: exclusion zone is barricaded and all occupants below have been notified and kept clear.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: water suppression system fails or dust extraction loses pressure — wait for repair and test before resuming.
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold platform becomes slippery or debris accumulation exceeds 50 mm — clear and dry platform before continuing.
🛑 STOP WORK if: asbestos-suspect material is identified — isolate, do not disturb, and tell site supervisor immediately.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain signed scaffold erection permit and handover certificate before any worker accesses scaffold.
Obtain working at heights permit signed by site supervisor before each elevated task.
Verify all workers hold valid White Card and current working at heights competency (RIIOHS204E or equivalent).
Obtain and display SDS for membrane product on site — brief all workers on contents before work starts.
Obtain EPA licence for on-site waste removal and segregation.
Obtain noise management plan from site supervisor — confirm neighbours and occupied units have been notified.
Record daily dust suppression system function check and HEPA filter condition in site logbook.
Conduct toolbox talk on silica dust hazards, fit-testing of respirators, and exclusion zone requirements before first shift.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) — fitted and sealed; fit-test each shift

monitoring.critical_control: Water suppression system running continuously and HEPA extraction filter pressure gauge in green zone.
monitoring.frequency: before each work phase and continuous during cutting
monitoring.evidence: Visual confirmation of water mist at cut point; filter saturation log; respirator fit-test record; exclusion zone barricade photographic record; waste segregation bin labels and daily removal records.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove existing waterproofing membrane, screed
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove existing waterproofing membrane, screed per SWMS

tasks.scope: Apply protective screed layer over membrane. Install tile bed substrate to falls and to engineer specification. Prepare surface for final tiling.
hazards: Inhalation of dust from dry screed mixing and application
Manual handling strain from carrying bags of screed and tile bed materials
Chemical irritation from cement and additives in screed product
Fall from height — slip from wet screed or mortar on working surface
Repetitive strain injury from trowelling and levelling operations
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — slip on wet screed or mortar during installation
controls: Wet screed surface with water spray before and during trowelling to reduce slip risk and dust generation.
Apply screed in layers not exceeding 50mm to engineer specification and allow adequate cure time between coats.
Install anti-slip tape or grit strips on scaffold platform edges and walkways where wet screed work occurs.
Mix screed in designated area away from scaffold edge — use portable mixer with dust extraction on site.
Wear respiratory protective equipment (P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) minimum) when mixing dry screed or applying powder additives.
Check membrane bond and substrate stability before screed application — stop work if membrane is damaged, lifting, or wet.
Remove excess wet screed and mortar from scaffold platform immediately after application to prevent slip hazard.
Limit working platform to maximum 3 workers per 4m² during wet screed application to manage slip risk and weight load.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply screed until: membrane has fully cured per manufacturer specification and engineer has signed off membrane installation
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start tiling until: screed has cured to minimum specification (14 days typical) and moisture test confirms surface is dry
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: membrane is visibly damaged, wet, or lifting before or during screed application
🛑 STOP WORK if: screed product SDS is not available on site or workers cannot confirm they have read SDS
🛑 STOP WORK if: wet screed or mortar accumulates on platform edges, guardrails, or walkways creating slip hazard
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain and display scaffold handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder before any worker accesses scaffold.
Obtain working at heights permit signed by supervisor before screed application commences each day.
Record scaffold daily inspection checklist on site — platform condition, guardrails, connections, tie-points.
Provide SDS for screed product and cement additives to all site workers — confirm receipt and understanding before work starts.
Brief all workers on wet surface slip hazard, maximum platform occupancy (3 workers per 4m²), and immediate cleanup of excess material.
tell building occupants of dust and noise from screed mixing — use local dust suppression and hearing protection.
Document screed cure time and moisture testing before tile bed application — engineer to verify readiness for next phase.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Respiratory protective equipment — P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) minimum (upgrade to P3 if dust extraction not available during mixing)

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: before each work period start and continuous during wet screed application
monitoring.evidence: Scaffold platform visual inspection record — note any wet material, condition of anti-slip tape, guardrail integrity. SDS acknowledgment sheet. Membrane cure certification and moisture test record. Daily scaffold inspection log.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Install screed and tile bed
responsibility.WKR: Perform Install screed and tile bed per SWMS

tasks.task: check slab and document crack condition
tasks.scope: Clean concrete slab. Identify, measure and photograph all cracks and spalling. Document defect locations and severity. Halt works pending Leo and Associates inspection approval before repair method confirmation.
hazards: Fall from height — slipping on wet or dusty slab surface at height
Inhalation of dust during slab cleaning and crack inspection
Eye injury from dust and debris during close inspection of crack detail
Manual handling strain from cleaning equipment and measurement tools
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — slip on uneven or contaminated slab surface
controls: Confirm scaffold handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder before any worker accesses platform.
Wet-clean slab surface with mop and water before inspection to suppress dust and reduce slip risk.
Wear eye protection
Use dust mask (P2) when dry-sweeping residual dust from crack surfaces.
Measure cracks with steel rule or crack-width gauge; photograph each defect with date and location label visible.
Do not work alone on scaffold — maintain two-person minimum during inspection work.
Brief all occupants before starting — noise, dust, and access restrictions; provide contact number for questions.
Stop work and clear platform if slab becomes wet from rain or building water sources.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not begin crack documentation until: scaffold handover certificate is signed and posted at base, and slab surface has been wet-cleaned and allowed to dry
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: slab surface becomes wet or slippery and cannot be dried within 10 minutes
🛑 STOP WORK if: weather deteriorates to rain, or building water ingress wets the platform
🛑 STOP WORK if: crack defects indicate structural concern (wide cracks >5mm, vertical step offset, active movement) — await Leo and Associates engineer visual before proceeding
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain and display scaffold handover certificate before work starts.
Confirm working at heights permit is current and posted on site.
Provide occupant briefing sheet covering dust, noise, and access lock-off.
Record all defect locations, crack widths, spalling areas, and severity ratings on site defect plan.
Photograph all cracks with date, location reference, and measurement scale visible.
Submit inspection report and photos to Leo and Associates for defect repair approval before scheduling repair method.
Log all work activity, platform conditions, and weather in site diary.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.frequency: before each shift starts and before scaffold is occupied
monitoring.evidence: Signed handover certificate posted at base and sighted by supervisor; platform inspection checklist completed and retained on file

responsibility.SUP: Supervise repairs, check scaffold safety, approve debris controls, sign hold points
responsibility.WKR: Perform repairs per SWMS, wear PPE, use dust control, report defects

tasks.scope: Fill and grind cracks per engineer recommendation. Repair spalled areas. Prepare slab to waterproofing substrate standard. Allow full cure before membrane application.
hazards: Inhalation of silica dust and filler particulates during crack filling and grinding
Chemical burn or skin sensitisation from epoxy or polyurethane repair products
Respiratory irritation from volatile organic compounds (VOCs) during product application
Noise and vibration exposure from grinding equipment
Fall from height — loss of balance during repair work and grinding operations
tasks.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of silica dust and chemical fumes during crack filling and grinding
controls: Obtain and review engineer recommendation for crack filling and repair method before starting work.
Wet grind using shrouded grinding equipment with integral water suppression and dust extraction to suppress silica dust at source.
Use local exhaust ventilation (LEV) or portable dust extractor on grinder discharge — position extraction hose within 300mm of grinding point.
Apply chemical filler products only in naturally ventilated or mechanically ventilated spaces — no enclosed work without active fume extraction.
Read safety data sheet (SDS) for epoxy, polyurethane, or cement-based filler before opening containers — brief all workers on VOC hazards and emergency procedures.
Barricade slab work area to exclude occupants — display 'Wet Grinding in Progress' signage at all entry points and on floors below.
Confirm scaffold handover certificate signed by licensed scaffolder and dated within current month before any worker enters work platform.
check scaffold condition — check all braces, connections, and guardrails tight and undamaged — stop work if any defect found.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start grinding until: wet suppression system is running, dust extraction confirmed active, and SDS briefing recorded for all present workers.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply chemical filler until: substrate is dry, ventilation is running continuously, and spill containment (drip tray or absorbent mat) is in place.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: grinding equipment water supply fails, dust extractor loses suction, or grinding continues dry without suppression.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any worker reports dizziness, respiratory distress, or chemical burn during filler application — evacuate and seek medical advice.
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold handover certificate cannot be located, is unsigned, or is dated over 30 days before work start.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain EPA air emissions licence (Category 31 — Coating or sealing operations) before telling occupied building occupants of work schedule.
Issue noise management plan to building manager — identify work hours, expected noise level, and commitment to minimise disturbance to occupied areas.
Record SDS review and hazard briefing in site diary — name attendees, date, and signature of supervisor.
Conduct toolbox talk on VOC symptoms (headache, nausea, respiratory irritation) and emergency response (evacuate, call emergency services, inform supervisor).
Confirm all workers hold current White Card (CPCCWHS1001) and Working at Heights competency (RIIOHS204E or equivalent) — retain copy on file before work commences.
Obtain signed Working at Heights permit from site manager and appointed competent supervisor before first day of elevated work.
Arrange dust and fume monitoring at start of each shift using portable equipment or by competent external monitor — record results daily.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Respiratory protective equipment — P2 particulate respirator (AS/NZS 1716) minimum during active grinding; upgrade to P3 or supplied air if airborne dust concentration exceeds workplace exposure standard.
eye protection— clear polycarbonate or tinted shade 5 to protect eyes from grinding sparks and filler splash.
Hearing protection — foam earplugs (SNR 27–33 dB minimum) or earmuffs during grinding operations.
High-visibility vest — orange or yellow Class D to remain visible to occupants and other workers on the building.
steel-capped footwear— steel-capped boots to AS/NZS 2210 minimum.
Cotton or natural-fibre work clothing — to avoid static buildup during chemical application; no synthetic fabrics that may trap chemical vapour.

monitoring.critical_control: Confirm wet grinding water suppression running and dust extractor suction active before each shift and after any pause exceeding 15 minutes.
monitoring.frequency: before shift start, after each break, before any change of operator
monitoring.evidence: Daily equipment checklist signed by supervisor; dust extractor filter visual check (no blockage or bypass); water flow visual confirmation at grinding point; air monitoring results recorded in site diary.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise repairs, check scaffold safety, approve debris controls, sign hold points
responsibility.WKR: Perform repairs per SWMS, wear PPE, use dust control, report defects

tasks.task: Lay and grout final tiles and finishes
tasks.scope: Install finish tiles to balcony surfaces. Grout and seal all joints. Reinstate balustrades and edge trims per original design. Final clean and make good.
hazards: Cut and laceration from tile cutting and sharp tile edges
Inhalation of silica dust from tile cutting
Manual handling strain from carrying tiles and grout bags to height
Chemical irritation from grout and sealant products
Fall from height — trip on tile materials or tools on working platform
Repetitive strain injury from tiling and grouting work
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — trip hazard from tile materials and equipment on platform
controls: Establish 2m exclusion zone around balcony edge before laying tiles — prevent unauthorised entry.
Check scaffold handover certificate and load calculation match tile and grout material weight before loading platform.
Wet-cut tiles using water suppression or dust extractor — do not dry-cut on platform.
Remove tile cutting equipment and offcuts from platform at end of each shift — eliminate trip hazard.
Review SDS for grout and sealant product before work starts — identify chemical hazards and ventilation needs.
Apply grout with mechanical mixer on ground, not on platform — reduce manual handling and fall risk.
Barricade platform edge with physical barrier if balustrade removed during reinstatement — maintain edge protection.
Isolate sealant product in well-ventilated area or use respirator approved for solvent vapour if indoor application required.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start tile laying until: scaffold handover certificate sighted, exclusion zone signage installed, and platform clear of trip hazards.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply sealant until: occupied building entry points isolated, ventilation confirmed or respirator fit-tested, and SDS reviewed with all workers.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: water suppression system fails during tile cutting — do not resume dry-cutting.
🛑 STOP WORK if: grout or sealant chemical irritation reported by any worker — isolate product and review SDS match.
🛑 STOP WORK if: balustrade removal exposes unprotected edge and no physical barrier installed within 5 minutes.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain current SDS for grout and sealant product — verify WorkSafe-approved version before delivery.
Confirm scaffolder holds current class-appropriate scaffolding licence — sighted before handover.
Obtain signed working at heights permit for each day elevated work occurs — kept on site during work.
Brief workers on occupied building protocols — restrict noise generation 8am–5pm weekdays, use low-noise cutting where possible.
Record final clean-up completion and trip hazard removal before handover to occupant — photograph platform clear state.
ppe: eye protection— impact-rated for tile cutting debris.
Dust mask P2 or powered respirator with organic vapour cartridge — selected per SDS chemical hazards.
Steel-capped boots — grip sole to reduce slip on wet platform.
hi-viz shirt or vest— protect skin from grout and sealant splash.

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: before each shift start, mid-shift spot check, after water suppression or sealant application
monitoring.evidence: Daily site checklist signed by supervisor; photographic record of cleared platform at shift end; SDS and scaffold handover certificate held on site.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Lay and grout final tiles
responsibility.WKR: Perform Lay and grout final tiles per SWMS

tasks.scope: Apply membrane per system manufacturer specification and engineer design. make sure full coverage, seams, edge details and penetration waterproofing. Obtain Leo and Associates inspection sign-off on completed membrane before screed application.
hazards: Inhalation of solvent vapours and chemical fumes from membrane product application
Skin contact and chemical burn from waterproofing membrane material
Respiratory sensitisation from isocyanates or other reactive chemicals in coating system
Fall from height — slip from wet or chemical-treated surface
Inadequate membrane coverage creating undetected water ingress pathways
tasks.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of toxic chemical fumes during membrane application
controls: Obtain and review manufacturer SDS for membrane product before application starts.
Establish continuous mechanical ventilation across application area — extract fumes to atmosphere, do not recirculate.
Check atmospheric conditions — do not apply if wind speed exceeds 5 m/s or rain forecast within 4 hours.
Apply membrane using supplied applicator method — follow system manufacturer specification for coverage, spread rate, and cure time.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves and replace every 30 minutes or after contact with membrane material.
Wear respiratory protection — Type P2 half-mask respirator with organic vapour cartridge during application and 30 minutes post-application.
Brief all workers on isocyanate sensitisation risk and symptoms — headache, chest tightness, asthma-like reaction.
Barricade application area — restrict entry to personnel involved in membrane work only.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start membrane application until: SDS reviewed, ventilation extraction confirmed running, and atmospheric conditions checked safe
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply screed until: Leo and Associates inspection sign-off obtained and recorded
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: ventilation extraction fails or is switched off during application or 30-minute post-application period
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker reports respiratory symptoms, headache, or chest tightness during or immediately after membrane application
🛑 STOP WORK if: visual inspection of membrane coverage shows gaps, thin spots, or incomplete seam overlap before cure completes
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Confirm scaffolding handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder before elevated work.
Verify working at heights permit and competency (RIIOHS204E) for all elevated workers.
Record SDS training and isocyanate sensitisation briefing for each worker before application.
Photograph completed membrane coverage and seams before inspection call — retain as evidence.
tell building occupants of chemical odour and ventilation requirements during application.
Check wind speed and weather forecast before application — record proceed or defer decision.
Keep SDS and manufacturer application guide on site and accessible during work.

Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Type P2 half-mask respirator with organic vapour cartridge — fit-tested and user-trained

monitoring.critical_control: Ventilation extraction running and worker respiratory check each 15 minutes
monitoring.frequency: every 15 minutes during application and post-application period
monitoring.evidence: Extraction fan operating visually confirmed; worker verbally confirms no respiratory symptoms

responsibility.SUP: Supervise membrane application, verify controls in place, sign off hold points

tasks.scope: Carry out final inspection with Leo and Associates. Document and fix any defects or non-conformances. Obtain final approval before scaffold release.
hazards: Fall from height — movement across incomplete or partially repaired balcony surface
Trip and fall from unfixed balustrades or temporary edge protection
Exposure to defective waterproofing during inspection allowing water contact
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — trip on temporary repairs or incomplete edge protection
controls: Check scaffold structure for stability before starting inspection — look for loose connections, bent tubes, or missing bracing.
Verify all edge protection is in place and secure before moving across work area — temporary repairs must be fixed, not loose.
Walk inspection route slowly — stop and wait if surface is wet, uneven, or has temporary patches.
Document each defect photographically and on defect sheet with location, description, and severity before fixing.
Barricade or rope off incomplete repairs or damaged areas — prevent pedestrian or worker passage until fixed.
Use only approved waterproofing product per SDS during rectification — apply in dry conditions only.
Allow waterproofing membrane minimum cure time per product instructions before final inspection — do not accelerate drying.
Confirm with Leo and Associates inspector that all documented defects are rectified to specification before scaffold release sign-off.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not release scaffold until: final approval certificate from Leo and Associates is signed and filed
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: edge protection is incomplete, missing, or unstable and defect repair is not in progress
🛑 STOP WORK if: waterproofing is wet and worker movement across membrane is required
🛑 STOP WORK if: balustrade or temporary edge guard is loose, unfixed, or trip hazard
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Brief all workers on defect locations and temporary repair zones before starting inspection.
Maintain defect register with photograph, location, repair method, and approval sign-off for each item.
Confirm waterproofing product SDS is on site and all personnel applying product have read it.
tell building occupants of inspection timing and temporary edge protection changes.
tell scaffolder and competent person of any scaffold alterations or temporary bracing added during rectification.
Store all approval certificates and defect records on site until handover completion.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Eye protection if applying waterproofing product

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.frequency: before each inspection shift and after any repair completion
monitoring.evidence: Defect sheet photo, edge protection check record, final approval certificate signed by Leo and Associates inspector

responsibility.WKR: Inspect per specification, photograph defects, report issues

task_blocks_raw.scope: Fill and grind cracks per engineer recommendation. Repair spalled areas. Prepare slab to waterproofing substrate standard. Allow full cure before membrane application.
hazards: Inhalation of silica dust and filler particulates during crack filling and grinding
Chemical burn or skin sensitisation from epoxy or polyurethane repair products
Respiratory irritation from volatile organic compounds (VOCs) during product application
Noise and vibration exposure from grinding equipment
Fall from height — loss of balance during repair work and grinding operations
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of silica dust and chemical fumes during crack filling and grinding
controls: Obtain and review engineer recommendation for crack filling and repair method before starting work.
Wet grind using shrouded grinding equipment with integral water suppression and dust extraction to suppress silica dust at source.
Use local exhaust ventilation (LEV) or portable dust extractor on grinder discharge — position extraction hose within 300mm of grinding point.
Apply chemical filler products only in naturally ventilated or mechanically ventilated spaces — no enclosed work without active fume extraction.
Read safety data sheet (SDS) for epoxy, polyurethane, or cement-based filler before opening containers — brief all workers on VOC hazards and emergency procedures.
Barricade slab work area to exclude occupants — display 'Wet Grinding in Progress' signage at all entry points and on floors below.
Confirm scaffold handover certificate signed by licensed scaffolder and dated within current month before any worker enters work platform.
check scaffold condition — check all braces, connections, and guardrails tight and undamaged — stop work if any defect found.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start grinding until: wet suppression system is running, dust extraction confirmed active, and SDS briefing recorded for all present workers.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply chemical filler until: substrate is dry, ventilation is running continuously, and spill containment (drip tray or absorbent mat) is in place.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: grinding equipment water supply fails, dust extractor loses suction, or grinding continues dry without suppression.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any worker reports dizziness, respiratory distress, or chemical burn during filler application — evacuate and seek medical advice.
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold handover certificate cannot be located, is unsigned, or is dated over 30 days before work start.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

ppe: Respiratory protective equipment — P2 particulate respirator (AS/NZS 1716) minimum during active grinding; upgrade to P3 or supplied air if airborne dust concentration exceeds workplace exposure standard.
eye protection— clear polycarbonate or tinted shade 5 to protect eyes from grinding sparks and filler splash.
Hearing protection — foam earplugs (SNR 27–33 dB minimum) or earmuffs during grinding operations.
High-visibility vest — orange or yellow Class D to remain visible to occupants and other workers on the building.
steel-capped footwear— steel-capped boots to AS/NZS 2210 minimum.
Cotton or natural-fibre work clothing — to avoid static buildup during chemical application; no synthetic fabrics that may trap chemical vapour.

task_blocks_raw.scope: Apply membrane per system manufacturer specification and engineer design. make sure full coverage, seams, edge details and penetration waterproofing. Obtain Leo and Associates inspection sign-off on completed membrane before screed application.
hazards: Inhalation of solvent vapours and chemical fumes from membrane product application
Skin contact and chemical burn from waterproofing membrane material
Respiratory sensitisation from isocyanates or other reactive chemicals in coating system
Fall from height — slip from wet or chemical-treated surface
Inadequate membrane coverage creating undetected water ingress pathways
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of toxic chemical fumes during membrane application
controls: Obtain and review manufacturer SDS for membrane product before application starts.
Establish continuous mechanical ventilation across application area — extract fumes to atmosphere, do not recirculate.
Check atmospheric conditions — do not apply if wind speed exceeds 5 m/s or rain forecast within 4 hours.
Apply membrane using supplied applicator method — follow system manufacturer specification for coverage, spread rate, and cure time.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves and replace every 30 minutes or after contact with membrane material.
Wear respiratory protection — Type P2 half-mask respirator with organic vapour cartridge during application and 30 minutes post-application.
Brief all workers on isocyanate sensitisation risk and symptoms — headache, chest tightness, asthma-like reaction.
Barricade application area — restrict entry to personnel involved in membrane work only.

🛑 STOP WORK if: visual inspection of membrane coverage shows gaps, thin spots, or incomplete seam overlap before cure completes

Manual handling strain from carrying bags of screed and tile bed materials
Chemical irritation from cement and additives in screed product
Fall from height — slip from wet screed or mortar on working surface
Repetitive strain injury from trowelling and levelling operations
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — slip on wet screed or mortar during installation
controls: Wet screed surface with water spray before and during trowelling to reduce slip risk and dust generation.
Apply screed in layers not exceeding 50mm to engineer specification and allow adequate cure time between coats.
Install anti-slip tape or grit strips on scaffold platform edges and walkways where wet screed work occurs.
Mix screed in designated area away from scaffold edge — use portable mixer with dust extraction on site.
Wear respiratory protective equipment (P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) minimum) when mixing dry screed or applying powder additives.
Check membrane bond and substrate stability before screed application — stop work if membrane is damaged, lifting, or wet.
Remove excess wet screed and mortar from scaffold platform immediately after application to prevent slip hazard.
Limit working platform to maximum 3 workers per 4m² during wet screed application to manage slip risk and weight load.

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start tiling until: screed has cured to minimum specification (14 days typical) and moisture test confirms surface is dry

task_blocks_raw.scope: Install finish tiles to balcony surfaces. Grout and seal all joints. Reinstate balustrades and edge trims per original design. Final clean and make good.
hazards: Cut and laceration from tile cutting and sharp tile edges
Inhalation of silica dust from tile cutting
Manual handling strain from carrying tiles and grout bags to height
Chemical irritation from grout and sealant products
Fall from height — trip on tile materials or tools on working platform
Repetitive strain injury from tiling and grouting work
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — trip hazard from tile materials and equipment on platform
controls: Establish 2m exclusion zone around balcony edge before laying tiles — prevent unauthorised entry.
Check scaffold handover certificate and load calculation match tile and grout material weight before loading platform.
Wet-cut tiles using water suppression or dust extractor — do not dry-cut on platform.
Remove tile cutting equipment and offcuts from platform at end of each shift — eliminate trip hazard.
Review SDS for grout and sealant product before work starts — identify chemical hazards and ventilation needs.
Apply grout with mechanical mixer on ground, not on platform — reduce manual handling and fall risk.
Barricade platform edge with physical barrier if balustrade removed during reinstatement — maintain edge protection.
Isolate sealant product in well-ventilated area or use respirator approved for solvent vapour if indoor application required.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start tile laying until: scaffold handover certificate sighted, exclusion zone signage installed, and platform clear of trip hazards.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply sealant until: occupied building entry points isolated, ventilation confirmed or respirator fit-tested, and SDS reviewed with all workers.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: water suppression system fails during tile cutting — do not resume dry-cutting.
🛑 STOP WORK if: grout or sealant chemical irritation reported by any worker — isolate product and review SDS match.
🛑 STOP WORK if: balustrade removal exposes unprotected edge and no physical barrier installed within 5 minutes.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
